items.title: Mrs. Samuel Pervaiz at Hunter Memorial Church, Sialkot
items.caption: Mrs. Samuel Pervaiz, wife of Bishop Samuel Pervaiz, the 3rd Bishop of Sialkot and Moderator of the Church of Pakistan, has devoted many years to the service of the Church.She actively served in the Women’s Fellowship of the Diocese and also contributed to the fields of nursing, women’s ministry, and youth work.She currently resides in Sialkot. This recent photograph was taken at Hunter Memorial Church, Sialkot, where she distributed gifts to young people who had successfully passed their Matriculation examinations.Her dedicated services in nursing, Women’s Fellowship, and youth ministry will long be remembered and appreciated.

items.title: Bishop Armstunz
items.caption: Bishop Armstunz served as Bishop of the United Methodist Church in Pakistan until 1968. He faithfully served the Church and the people of Pakistan, dedicating his ministry to the glory of God. A life of faithful service, remembered with gratitude. “Well done, good and faithful servant.” — Matthew 25:23 (Transcribed from Facebook caption · spelling Armstunz kept as in caption; claims may need cross-check.)

items.title: Bishop & Mrs. Johnston Safdar Qadir Bakhsh
items.caption: Bishop & Mrs. Johnston Safdar Qadir Bakhsh. Constitutional Leader • Great Reformer • Pioneer of the Church of Pakistan. Bishop Johnston Safdar Qadir Bakhsh played a significant role in strengthening the constitutional framework and indigenous leadership of the Church of Pakistan. 1. Reform of Episcopal Elections. He advocated reforms in the Rules for the Election of Bishops, introducing clearer standards of qualification, fitness, experience, and the voice of the people in the selection of church leadership. 2. Reorganisation of the Church. During his leadership, the structure of the Church of Pakistan was strengthened and reorganised, with four new dioceses created to expand and improve the Church’s ministry and administration. His vision was rooted in responsible leadership, constitutional order, indigenous participation, and a stronger Church for future generations.
items.alt: Colour outdoor full-length portrait of a clergyman in a purple cassock with a pectoral cross standing beside a woman in a white sari with a green blouse, in front of green foliage.
items.sourceLabel: Facebook page History: Church of Pakistan

items.title: Hyderabad Diocese established, 1980 · Bishop Bashir Jewan
items.caption: In 1980, the Hyderabad Diocese of the Church of Pakistan was formally established, with Bishop Bashir Jewan, who was elected in the first ballot, becoming its inaugural bishop. He was consecrated as Bishop of Hyderabad by Bishop Johnston Safdar Qadir Bakhsh. The Diocese of Hyderabad has had subsequent bishops, including Bishop Smart K Das and Bishop Rafiq Masih, and is currently led by Bishop Kaleem John, who also serves as Deputy Moderator of the Church of Pakistan and is now one of the Senior Bishops of the Church of Pakistan.
items.alt: Four-panel colour collage of portraits of the same clergyman at different ages in white or maroon vestments with stoles and pectoral crosses, arranged in a two-by-two grid.
items.sourceLabel: Facebook page History: Church of Pakistan
items.contextNote: Public-record / press context (allegations reported by Dawn · not proven court findings): In a Dawn report headlined “HYDERABAD: Builder mafia occupies church property: bishop,” then-Bishop Rafiq Masih alleged that a builder mafia occupied Church of Pakistan property in Sukkur in collusion with former bishop Bashir Jeewan and his children Naureen Mirza and John Jeewan. The report said a mission bungalow was taken via a fake attorney and sold, with builders demolishing the site; it also claimed earlier occupation of St. Xavier School, Sukkur (later recovered by the diocese, per Masih). The matter was said to be in the civil court of Sukkur. This site records those newspaper-reported allegations with citations; it does not treat them as adjudicated facts or judge individuals. Office dates (Wikipedia): Rt. Rev. Bashir Jiwan is listed as first Bishop of Hyderabad, 1981–1997. Facebook captions on this card are kept verbatim as Family Archive provenance; honorific wording (e.g. “Great Leader”) and the “8th Moderator” claim are caption claims and are not independently verified here.
